cohort: 180 pregnant women at Vani Vilas Hospital and Bowring & Lady Curzon Hospital, BMCRI, Bangalore
finding: Transcervical Foley's catheter had a shorter induction-delivery interval, lower rate of caesarean section, and fewer NICU admissions compared to intravaginal misoprostol and intracervical dinoprostone.
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery rates were 76.7% for misoprostol, 68.3% for dinoprostone, and 83.3% for Foley's catheter.
